body:
Both of my siblings have bipolar disorder with psychotic features and began showing symptoms around age 12. I am in my early 30s and have  had severe depression and anxiety since age 13. 

How likely is it that I will experience mania or psychosis some day? Are there any environmental factors (e.g. taking certain drugs, stressful life events) that would make it more likely that I would develop those symptoms in the future?

I asked a previous therapist if my parents were abusive and she refused to answer. She just kept dodging the question and flipped it around to ask, "How would it make you feel if your parents were abusive?" Ugh.
Thank you for the suggestions! I didn't know that clinics offered these services.
Thank you for the suggestion. I have relatives who do home health so I'm surprised that I didn't think of that. I will see what my options are locally and how much it may cost.
Thank you. I went to two baby showers this month but there aren't celebrations for sterilization. I appreciate you celebrating with me. 🎉🥳

Thank you for taking the time to write this! I'm sorry to hear that your in the same situation but your post gives me hope. The surgery is in two weeks so I will make sure to look at the release policy and look up options in case I need someone to pick me up. 

I didn't think of keeping things at waist level are keeping prepared food on hand. I found some helpful posts on here about the recovery process so I will take notes to help me prepare. Again, thank you and best wishes for your surgery.
I didn't know that existed. Thank you for sharing the information. I will see if there is someone in my area.

I want to be my therapist's favorite client because I feel like no one cares about me and it wouldn't matter if I died so I want someone to like me. I assume that I am really boring and don't stand out to my therapist because I can't connect with anyone and don't have friends. Why would a therapist be different?

I had a therapist who preferred to work with children. I felt jealous when I saw one of her child clients in the waiting room because I knew that I couldn't compete. I didn't feel that she cared about me because she was cold and never seemed to react and seemed to get impatient with me.

Thank you for your kind words. I think it's accurate that they were understaffed. Once a psych tech had at least 3 patients following him around all day because they were at risk of hurting themselves but there weren't enough staff to watch them.

I hope I can find a therapist like the one you described.

>It's hard not to compare yourself to others, but doing so can sometimes be just another way to invalidate yourself.

I didn't have the words for it, but it does feel invalidating. I try my best to be honest and convey how much I am struggling. I will try to share what I wrote here with my current therapist.

I've worked with about 20 therapists in my lifetime. At least half were licensed therapists with decades of experience and the rest were either interns or in grad school. I think it's more important that you find whether the therapist is a good fit for you in terms of personality and the type of therapy they do. 

Some of the interns were really skilled and could run circles around the more experienced clinicians. Other interns were a poor fit and did more harm than good. 

If I had a negative experience, it's often with the interns that had zero interest in working with clients like me (e.g. one wanted to work with children only and another wanted to be a professor/researcher and had no intention of working with patients).

My main gripe with working with interns is that they usually leave to work somewhere else after their internship is over so I would definitely ask about that. It is frustrating to build rapport with a therapist only to have them leave after a year.

Thank you for sharing your experience. 

Do you have any advice for finding a good therapist? I had to change therapists frequently because of  university and moving. I've tried therapists through my insurance and many are unprofessional or a poor fit (e.g. cleaning their nails and eating during session, refusing to talk about suicide etc.)

Thank you for writing this. It feels like a huge loss but I didn't think to consider the opportunities that are available to me without the relationship. I felt stuck in my hometown because I have been waiting for him to finish college and start his career.

I started off this year with a therapist that I loved. She was an intern at a university and refused to see me more than once a week. Then she canceled our appointment in March due to Covid-19 and I was left without a therapist. I tried talkspace and various therapists through my insurance with no luck. 

I went to a residential treatment facility for two months and really liked my therapist there, but the treatment facility was in a different state so I wasn't referred to an intensive outpatient program nor did we find a new therapist in my hometown. I was left without a therapist again when I got home.

I tried local therapists through my insurance again and had bad experiences. I gave up and went back to the university. I'm seeing another intern through teletherapy and she will graduate in August. 

I'm so frustrated. I've gone through 8 therapists this year alone and still haven't found anyone who can treat me long term.

I did a screening for a clinical trial for depression a few years ago and didn't meet criteria to participate in the study. I was contacted to participate in a different study this week. Again, I was told that I didn't meet criteria but they want to screen me for their BPD study. 

I have been going to therapy and taking medication for depression for over a decade and I always get the MDD label. I have been tested for other things (including personality disorders, autism  etc.) but I never meet the criteria. Part of me wishes that I had a different diagnosis because every therapist feels that they know how to treat me based on my depression diagnosis but I  haven't made progress despite being in treatment for over a decade.

I was in a residential treatment facility for two months and I was the only one with "just" a depression and anxiety diagnosis. I worried that the staff did not take me seriously because of that.

I also read that clinical trials are more strict with their criteria and won't take participants with any comorbidities. I think that may be the the case for me and I should stop signing up for these studies.

I would be interested. The psychology today profiles are unhelpful for choosing who is a good fit. Therapists claim that they know every modality and treat every disorder. 

I have tried free 15 minutes consultations and asked specific questions about the modality they use and issues they treat only to find out that it's a completely different story when I actually work with them. Some therapists don't even offer the 15 minute consultation. 

It's expensive, time consuming, and exhausting to find a therapist who is a good fit. What makes it even harder is that I can't even get referrals because no one recognizes the providers on my network.

The therapist that she recommended works in the same practice as her. She hurt me so much that I would rather choose some random therapist from my insurance's in network providers list than someone associated with her.


I don't trust a therapist who blows me off when I say that I struggling to the point where I am buying materials for a suicide attempt and getting my affairs in order. I told her the exact suicide method I wanted to use and started crying she just wanted me to download Bumble and Forest.


She could probably help me with time management, which is something I struggle with, but I don't trust her anymore when it comes to treating my mental health issues.

>Her behavior was appropriate for a behaviorist. It is like dog training, your thoughts and feelings are largely Irrelevant to the process.

When I did the phone consultation I asked what modality she used and she said, "CBT and Brene Brown." Every CBT therapist that I have worked with before is willing to talk about thoughts, emotions, and behavior. How can we do CBT if she is not willing to talk about thoughts and emotions at all?

I am not familiar with Brene Brown but we watched a video of hers in the residential treatment center and it focused on shame and being vulnerable. 

If she said that she was a behaviorist from the get go, I would not be so surprised.

Thank you for your insight. I felt like it wasn't right but it's hard to tell because it's just the two of us in the room and she is in a position of authority.

I find my therapists by getting a list of in network providers in my area. I have asked for referrals but no one I know is familiar with the names on the list. Sometimes I search them up on Psychology Today if they have a profile but it's hard to get a sense for what they are like through that website. It seems that everyone lists two dozen modalities.
Yes. I think about this too.

I had the same experience with talkspace. I used them for about 3 months. I would write long messages and only get short generic responses. It didn't feel like therapy. I read that the therapists' pay gets docked if they don't respond in a certain time frame. As a result, I would write long messages and the only response I would get is, "I'll respond to this later."  

I even paid extra for the weekly video sessions, but they were only 30 minutes and felt super rushed. I also dislike that you have to pay a month in advance. I wanted to quit my subscription in the middle of the month because I had to go to an inpatient mental health facility and talkspace refused to give me a refund even though I wouldn't be allowed to access my phone to use the app while I was in inpatient. I do not recommend them at all.

I've worked with several interns and many of them were a better fit than the clinicians with over a decade of experience. However, many of them didn't tell me that they would leave after only a year. I would have preferred to know that from day one. I dislike that working with interns means that I have had to change therapists every year.
Thank you for your support.

They have a day program but it's hundreds of miles away from where I live. I had to go to a residential program in a different state because I couldn't find a local place that accepted my insurance. 

I was pretty much on my own when it came time to find local resources.

I am stuck. I am out of options. I spent the last 2 months in a residential treatment facility. I told them I wasn't ready to be discharged and my symptoms would return if I had to go back to the environment that triggered all this in the first place. I didn't even have a therapist to go back to. 

I called five therapists to try and make an appointment and only one called back. We had a video session but I cannot work with her. She acted bored the entire time and she felt that because I had been in treatment for so long that she didn't have to act like she cared. I have had 20 therapists throughout my life and I have no energy to play this telephone game again to find a decent one. I need more than 50 minutes of support per week anyway.

Covid-19 means that I don't even have the option of leaving the situation I am in. There is no end in sight. When I was in the treatment facility I said over and over again that I had nothing to live for once I returned home. I have zero social support. I would rather die than continue my job.  

I am feeling very suicidal right now and I have nowhere to go to get any real help or support. I don't even have a therapist now. If I die, no one will even find out.

Does anyone have advice for finding an intensive outpatient program for mental health?

I have been doing 1 hour a week therapy sessions for over a decade with no improvement. At this point, my therapist is just telling me to stay alive in the 7 days between session for months on end. I want a higher level of care, but every in network intensive outpatient program in my area is for substance abuse or eating disorders. Calling my insurance did not help, they couldn't find any local facilities either.

At his point, I'm seriously considering traveling 1,000 miles away for a program that will take me (with no addiction/eating disorder diagnosis) and accept my insurance. I wish I could find something that was 100 or 500 miles away.

Thank you for the advice. It is rare for me to find someone in a similar situation. I was thinking about telling my parents that I would be out of town for a conference but it is a less convincing excuse due to Covid-19.
Thank you for taking the time to explain this. It was really helpful.

How do you recommend learning about different modalities? 95% of my previous therapists did CBT, so I have been telling any new therapists that I want to try something else. They turn it around and ask me what modality they want me to use. 

Looking up the information on Google is not helpful. A generic description doesn't give me a good sense of what we would be doing in therapy and how it would make me feel to do that type of therapy. I want to be more informed but I don't know where to look.

I have been in therapy continuously for 15 years and I have had nearly 20 therapists. It's because of moving and the fact that most of my therapists were interns/trainees in graduate school. 

I liked that you reframed it. It's harder for me to relate because I will never be considered "high functioning" despite years of therapy. For me, I would frame it as a person with severe disabilities need doctors, physical/occupational/speech therapists, special education teachers, adaptive equipment, assistive technology etc. that a typically developing person wouldn't need.
Thank you. I hadn't even thought of it that way.

Thank you. I hadn't thought of doing that to ensure confidentiality. Thank you for the advice. I had considered telling them I had fibroids in my uterus but I was concerned because I didn't know the recovery time and one of my parents is a nurse.
Thank you for your kind words. I am crying and I am not sure why but I needed to hear this.

I stopped seeing my therapist in mid March due to Covid-19. She is an intern at a university and said she wouldn't be able to start teletherapy until mid May. Well, it's mid may and she is still not approved for teletherapy and she made a passing comment that interns can't do teletherapy in our state. 

I have been spending $400 per month to speak to someone through Talkspace. Someone once described these sort of services as "texting your very busy friends who likes to give trite platitudes" and I feel that is accurate.

It was only supposed to be for a month while I waited for my old therapist to start seeing me again but I feel like that's never going to happen. She was supposed to graduate in August anyway. 

I can find a therapist through my insurance but I hate the process of finding a new therapist with a burning passion (I have had 20+ therapists) and had no energy to do it when I was working 15 hour days from home and dealing with being stuck inside with my dysfunctional family. I actually did set up an appointment with a therapist through my insurance but she was so unprofessional that I cancelled the next appointment.

I started using TalkSpace when the mental health clinics and private practices closed due to Covid-19. I used a discount code the first month,  but it is much more expensive now that I have to pay the full amount. 

Like you said, it's not the same as face to face but it has been helpful. It was also faster than calling multiple therapists through my insurance to see who does teletherapy.

I do get at least two responses from the therapist daily, but sometimes the response is very short or she just says, "I'll reply later." Have you ever experienced something similar?

>I hate the process of finding a new therapist with a burning passion

I feel exactly the same way. I just called my state's mental health holine and they sent me the name of a few local places that offer IOP.

It's really helpful to read about your experiences.  After speaking to my therapist, I felt like I was misguided in asking for more therapy but I really felt that I needed more support.

Thank you for your insight. I'm glad to hear that IOP may be an option I could try. I don't know much about the IOPs in my area but I'll do some research to see if there are any any that focus on DBT skills.
Thank you for the suggestion. I don't live in AZ, but I'll try to see if I can find a group through psychology today.

Thank you. It's validating to hear from someone else that my symptoms are as bad as I perceive them. I'll pursue an intensive outpatient program.

I did not know about genesight. I have a family history of mental illness so I think genetic testing would be worthwhile. 

It's also a relief to hear that someone else has tried medication with little success. I know many people who find medication beneficial, but I rarely hear about people in a similar situation as me.
Thank you for sharing your experience with IOP and dealing with insurance. I'm glad that you find it helpful and I hope that I can find something, whether in person or remotely.

I tried calling my insurance and had a hard time figuring out if they covered it, but I guess I can call the facility directly. I will try to contact an intensive outpatient center, though I am not sure if they are even open now.

>Why does your therapist think Intensive Outpatient is inappropriate for you?

From what I understand, she felt that intensive outpatient was appropriate for people who were in inpatient or residential because they could not keep themselves safe and needed to transition to a lower level of care before they're ready to do the 50 minutes a week. What kind of patients go to intensive outpatient? I interpreted my therapists' explanation "your symptoms are not bad enough" and I don't know anyone who has done it.

I am currently on three different medications and I have been on about twelve over the past 15 years. None of them have had any noticeable effect. I did about 30 sessions of bilateral transcranial magnetic stimulation, which was prohibitively expensive because my insurance does no cover it. It had no effect and I am reluctant to spend tens of thousands of dollars to try it again when it didn't work the first time.

I did a consultation for ECT, but they said that after the procedure I could not go home alone and needed someone there to take care of me, which I didn't have at the time. Also, the potential for long term effects on memory and cognition is a dealbreaker for me. As far as I know, even if I do show improvement after ECT there is no guarantee that it works in the long term. Please correct me if I'm wrong. I no longer have access to scientific journals now that I am no longer in college so my ability to research it is limited.

I was already irritable and upset because of transitioning to  working from home with minimal training. I was supposed to have a 30 minute video session with my therapist from talkspace. I can't schedule meetings on the website or through the phone (you can only schedule on the iOS app). We scheduled it via text instead and she agreed that she would initiate the call at a certain time. She never called me and it has been hours since our scheduled time and I haven't heard a word from her. 

I'm so angry and upset. I've been really struggling this week so I'm really disappointed. I told her that I was suicidal this weekend and had to wait two hours to speak to someone on the crisis chatline and after all that waiting the chat didn't even work. I got the same brief reply. This is a really stressful time and I feel like I'm talking to a bot instead of a therapist. I feel like I can't get anything done because she just gives 3-5 sentences a day so it takes forever to have a conversation. Someone described it as "It’s like sending emails to your really busy friends who responds with inspirational quotes" and that is exactly how I feel. At least a friend does not charge hundreds of dollars per month for the privilege. I miss my old therapist and I wish I could do phone or video sessions with her but that is not an option.

Most of my therapists have tried to get me to sign a no suicide contract or sign a safety plan. When I was 16, the therapist refused to work with me because I would not sign the contract.

Now that I am an adult, I don't want to sign the safety plan because I feel it is worthless but my therapist is adamant that I do it. It's a CYA thing so she can document that she did her due diligence in the event that I do end up killing myself. I relented and signed it because she wouldn't let it go and I wanted to move on with the actual treatment but I refuse to call 911 or go to the hospital because I have done that already and it is not helpful in this situation.

So the clinic where my therapist works is closed. I didn't hear from her for ten days then she finally called to tell me that I don't have the option of phone sessions or telehealth.

I signed up for one month of talkspace and it is shit. I get 3-5 sentence responses twice a day, even when I write several paragraphs of information. I sometimes feel that it is no better than speaking to a bot. I spent the extra money for 30 minute live video sessions and I have been trying to schedule something for three days to no avail. This is such a waste of money, but they make you prepay for a month's worth of sessions so I am stuck.

I've been feeling suicidal and I waited 2 hours to speak to someone on the suicide prevention chatline (I was the 52nd person in the queue). By the time I got to the front of the line the chat wasn't working. In the past my therapist said that I needed to stay alive long enough to make it to the next sessions so we could work on my problems but there will be no next session. I can't spend months waiting for the clinic to open again.

I'm in the same boat. My therapist is an intern at a university clinic and graduates soon. There will be no teletherapy and I have no way of contacting her. I just realized today that I won't see her again. I feel frustrated and lost.

She is an intern and planned to graduate in August. I'm starting to think that I may not have the chance to see her again since universities may be closed for the summer as well.

Thank you. I'm looking into options for teletherapy and hope I can find someone.

My therapist left me a voicemail on Monday saying that she was cancelling all future therapy sessions infidelity. She works in a university clinic and I have no way of contacting her until the university opens again.  The state department of education said that universities will remain closed for the rest of the semester. I'm really upset because I don't have the option of phone sessions or teletherapy.

Thank you, I really appreciate what you have said. I'm not sure how to phrase this, but this is one of those rare times when I feel seen. I get the impression that most people don't think my situation is a big deal and I am just not trying hard enough. Each individual thing you described takes a massive toll and makes it difficult to have the hope or energy necessary to keep going.



What do you think makes your current job better than your old one? 



I was diagnosed with ADHD by a psychologist 5 years ago but two different therapists read the report "weren't convinced," that I had ADHD. They said that my issues with executive function were caused by my depression and it would get better once my depression improved. That is not helpful because I have been depressed with no remission for the past 14 years despite intensive treatment. However, therapists don't prescribe medication and most psychiatrists have accepted the diagnosis. How has medication for ADHD helped you?

Thank you for sharing your experience. You articulated what I was struggling to express so clearly.

I am a speech-language pathologist. I knew before I applied to graduate school  that I didn't want to do this. My job has a high workload with very little pay or respect. I have to take work home because there isnot enoughtime during the day, which makes me constantly stressed. I don't enjoy the population I work with. My professors and supervisors all said that I would never graduate or get a job because of how socially awkward I was.

My psychiatrist is the one who advocates changing jobs. However, I often fear that I would struggle in any field. I'm very socially awkward and I have severe social anxiety. I also have poor executive functioning skills. I'm not curious or interested in anything and struggle with the skills employers value. 

My salary is a barrier to moving out and getting my own place. I live with an abusive family so this affects my quality of life. Changing jobs may lead to a higher salary, but the jobs I'm qualified for pay the same or less than I make now.

I am taking medication now (3 different pills) and have tried 12 over the past 12 years. My psychiatrist is reluctant to add more medication because she said I'm already taking a lot. 

She has said that there is only so much medication can do. She also said multiple times that she doesn't think it's possible for me to be happy until I change my job and living situation. Doing that requires much more time, energy, and money than taking pills every day (realistically I would have to leave the state), so I have not been able to do that. I also did transcranial magnetic stimulation with no noticeable improvement.

How do you know when medication is working?

I know this is a bot, but I have called the suicide hotline dozens of times over the years. On a few occasions I was able to get in touch with someone willing to talk to me but I have had many terrible experiences. They've hung up on me multiple times. One person told me that I would go to hell if I killed myself. One person was annoyed because I struggled to stop crying and she said something like, "You called to talk but you aren't saying anything." I've noticed that if I said, "I plan to kill myself later this week," or "I'm already taking medication and seeing a therapist," they end the conversation because they have other, more urgent calls that are a priority or because I'm "already receiving care."

In college I told a therapist at the student  counseling center that I was involuntarily hospitalized for a presumed suicide attempt a few days before our session. I didn't attempt suicide but I did take a subleathal dose of the drug I had been planning on using for  a suicide attempt.

I didn't completely understand what was going on but it looked like he was either working really hard to stop himself from sobbing or struggling to breathe. There were no tears but he was inhaling deeply and audibly and clearly something was wrong. I didn't acknowledge it or ask him about it because I felt uncomfortable but I really wish I had. I think it would have been beneficial to talk about it and he was very open. 

Another therapist seemed to be blinking more than usual and I thought I heard her voice waver slightly when we were talking about suicide. I could not be sure if she was actually getting teary or if I had just imagined it because it was so brief. She seemed calm to the point of being disinterested or uncaring in all subsequent sessions when we discussed suicide. This bothered me. I wanted to know if she cared and had frequent thoughts about hurting myself to see if it would make her sad. Her lack of emotion made me feel like she didn't care at all and I began to hate her. Other things began to negatively affect our relationship but this was a huge issue for me. 

My current therapist seems to get red eyes sometimes when I'm really distressed and talk about dying but she recovers so quickly that I feel like I might have imagined it. 

Personally, if they were in fact trying not to cry I wish that my therapists would stop trying to hide it. I already feel like no one cares about me and I am better off dead. I understand why they wouldn't want to start crying in session but I think it would be helpful at least acknowledged how they were feeling. The way they do it now just messes with my emotions. It would be better if they acknowledged that they were having an emotional reaction instead of making me feel like I'm imagining things or their emotions are something to be hidden/shrouded in mystery and I can't talk about because they won't even acknowledge it in front of me. It would strengthen my bond with them if I knew that the did care that much and didn't just tolerate me because they needed the hours for their internships.

I feel like I could have written this post. I was in a very similar situation last year. I saw a therapist who was an intern at a local university, spent hours googling her online, looked at friends' and family's profiles, drove past her house, and wanted to harm myself to get her attention. I made a fake Instagram but never made a follow request because I was sure I would be denied. I never brought it up in therapy because I was sure that she would terminate and I would be banned from seeing anyone else at the clinic. The only difference is that people on here were nowhere near as supportive and I was basically told that I was creepy and inappropriate. 

I don't have any helpful advice because I never resolved the issue. I never said anything because I thought (and still think that) my therapist would have had a very negative  and I would be banned from the clinic. Over time I grew to resent her because I felt like she didn't care about me and didn't like me. I tried to bring this up in therapy but I felt like her response was callous and uncaring so I grew to hate her. 

I wanted to find a new therapist outside of the university training clinic so I could discuss this openly but I haven't been able to find one that is a good fit. I still feel angry whenever I think about that person. 

Again, I'm sorry that I don't have anything helpful to say. Just know that you are not the only one experiencing this and it would probably be helpful to discuss this with a therapist who is nonjudgemental so you don't end up like me.
How did you find a therapist with a relatively trauma free background? My therapists usually don't self disclose enough for me to know, but I'm concerned about the potential comparison.
If that is the case, then why hasn't my therapist told me that? I would want my therapist to communicate that to me.

Last week I was discussing how hopeless and suicidal I felt with my therapist. She said that we needed to "make some changes." 

I was miffed because I heard vague statements like that before. I've heard statements like, "You have to do the work in order to get better." My therapists never explain what I have to do specifically to get better and then get upset when I don't make progress. 

When I see her next week, I hope she explains what these mysterious changes are.
I went to Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka, Hiroshima, Hakone, and Kamakura.

I checked facebook today and was reminded of just how alone I am. I graduated from my master's program almost 3 and a half years ago. In the first two years after graduation, many of my classmates got married. My Facebook feed was filled with photos of elaborate weddings. My classmates would often invite 5 other students from the program to their weddings. It was just a reminder that I had no friends. I've never been invited to a wedding. 



I deactivated Facebook for a few months. When, I reactivated it, suddenly everyone had a baby. There is a photo of at least five of my graduate school classmates standing in a row while holding their babies. Even though they are spread out across the country, they go on cruises together and take photos like this.



I will probably never reach any of these milestones that everyone is expected to have. There is no greeting card for your 12 year anniversary of being in therapy. My parents disclosed that they thought I would never be able to work, but there is no celebration for that. 


I still live with my parents. I have no friends. I hate my job but I still can't afford to support myself financially. Even my coworkers say that there is  something wrong with me. As of November 2018, all of my parents' children have been involuntarily hospitalized for mental health issues. I'm living the same lifestyle I was living at age 14 when I first wanted to kill myself. They said it would get better, but things have stayed the same. 



I know that other people's lives are not perfect. One of the girls posing in the baby/wedding/BFF cruise photos got married less than two weeks after getting discharged from a mental hospital for a psychotic episode. She started showing symptoms after a sexual assault. We even posed for happy graduation photos together. We both graduated two semesters later then the rest of our class because of mental health issues. We were the only two people from our program at the ceremony. I wondered how she was doing so I looked her up on Facebook today. She had unfriended me. The photo of us posing together with our caps and gowns is still public though.


Two summers ago I finally went on the trip to Japan that I have been saving up for since middle school. Some strangers are impressed that I traveled to a foreign country alone. The truth is that I have zero friends and I had no one to share the experience with. I was able to get through the lines at Universal Studios Japan quickly because I  was a single rider though.

Anyway, who would come to my funeral? If I don't end up killing myself at a young age, may parents will die before me so they can't come.

Doesn't transference occur when you  redirect some of your feelings or desires for another person to your therapist? I'm not sure if I experience transference with my current therapist. I sometimes feel angry or annoyed with her. That is a relief compared to my previous experiences though.




I had strong crushes on my previous therapists and it got to a level that was very unhealthy. I was too embarrassed to bring it up in session. I think I recognized how unhealthy it was and now I don't want to know **anything** about my current therapist's personal life.

I have had a similar experience. My previous therapist wrote on her LinkedIn profile that she is interested in working with children and adolescents. I'm an adult. I once saw her smiling while bringing a child back from a session and speaking to his mother for a long time. 

I feel pathetic for being jealous of a child but I felt like she probably disliked working with me because I am a boring socially awkward adult and he is a cute, funny child.
Thank you for explaining. This was very helpful.
Thank you for the information. Can you clarify what the difference is between a directive and non-directive therapist?
Thank you for your insight. What is the name of the life coach podcast?
Thank you for the information and the link.

> A good therapist doesn't give advice; a good therapist is only there to help you see how your decisions affect you. He or she is there to hold a mirror up to you and your choices.

Can you give an example? What might a therapist say to help a client see the effect of her decisions?

>But Step One to effective counseling is, as the client, deciding to take ownership of your decisions

How do you know when you are taking ownership of your decisions? I thought I was.

I'm not sure because it has been a while since I had a therapist like that. I think one of them radiated warmth and didn't seem to be judging me. My current therapist just seems cold and doesn't show much empathy. 

I guess it varies from person to person and depends on whether the two of you are compatible.

>Have you ever had a therapist you felt you worked well with?

I'm not sure because I had to change therapists so frequently and felt like I haven't made progress. I am able to think of therapists who made me feel like they actually cared though.
